name: shell
title: Shell
description: Run a command in your login shell and read what it printed in the panel: stdout in mono, stderr in red, the exit code and the duration. Typing never runs anything (Enter does), a command that looks destructive asks first, the output copies on Enter, opens in a terminal on cmd+Enter, runs again on cmd+r. A history of every command with its exit code.
author: pal

settings.label: Shell
settings.description: The shell and its flags; `$SHELL` is your login shell. `-l` loads the login profile (PATH), `-i` the interactive one (aliases); `-c` takes the command. A `zsh -lc` skips the aliases and the interactive noise.

settings.label: Timeout
settings.description: A command still running after this is killed (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and the view says so; what it printed until then is kept.

settings.label: Environment
settings.description: `KEY=VALUE` lines set for every command, on top of the host's environment.

settings.label: Confirm destructive commands
settings.text: Ask before running a command that removes, overwrites or escalates (rm, sudo, mv, dd, git reset --hard, ...)

settings.label: Terminal
settings.description: What cmd+Enter opens: `Terminal` (default), `iTerm`, `kitty`, `Alacritty`, `WezTerm`, `Ghostty`, or any app name (`open -na <name> --args -e ...`); on Linux a command name (`kitty`, `foot`, `alacritty`, `wezterm`, `ghostty`, ...), else `$TERMINAL`, else the first of those installed.

store.tagline: Run a command, read its output in the panel, run it again
features: One row until Enter: `Run: <command>`; typing runs nothing, and a command that looks destructive (`rm`, `sudo`, `mv`, `dd`, `git reset --hard`, ...) asks first
Runs in your login shell (`$SHELL -lic`), so PATH, aliases and functions from your rc files apply; `cwd`, `env` and `timeout` are settings
The output as a view: the command as the title, the exit code and the duration as badges, stdout in monospace on a sunken surface, stderr under it in red, scrolling past the panel
A command that outlasts the pick shows a running view with the elapsed time and the result lands in place when it ends; the timeout kills it and the view says so
Enter copies the output, cmd+Enter opens the command in a terminal (Terminal, iTerm, kitty, Alacritty, WezTerm, Ghostty), cmd+r runs it again, cmd+c copies the command
Shell History: every command with its exit code and duration, newest first; Enter runs it again
`$ ls` or `> git status` at the root lists the Run row inline
